cards.text: MOT-FURIOUS-VSL-01 — THE $300 CABINET (HEYGEN STORYBOARD)

cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: HeyGen talking-head VSL for Motilli, GLP-1 constipation angle, mirroring the Alicia Darling / Nuora ad (190 days running). Format law: face in a parked car for the whole ad, burned captions bottom-center 2-5 words, overlay cards ABOVE her head that appear and vanish in sync with the exact claim being spoken, and FULL-BLEED takeovers for the three big mechanism moments. Emotional driver is FURY at wasted money, not shame. Brand is not named until 5:45 of 6:00. OVERLAY DENSITY LAW: this is a majority-overlay ad - the bare talking head is the exception, not the default; every beat carries either an overlay card, avatar b-roll, or a full-bleed render, EXCEPT the single absolution beat which is deliberately bare. Two more non-negotiables: every failed-solution overlay uses REAL product packaging (never generic bottles), and every study card cites a REAL paper.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: If your belly looks like this, hips look like this, or chin looks like this, you need to see this.
Talking head in parked car. Small overlay card sits ABOVE her head: her own mirror-selfie of her midsection, then a stomach diagram. Burned caption bottom-center.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Recognition jolt — HOOK. Three body callouts = three chances to self-ID in 5 seconds.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Because I wasted five months and close to $300 on gut health supplements that did absolutely nothing.
Overlay: photo of the ACTUAL supplement bottles she bought, real labels visible (NutraVit 'Nutra Gut').

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Wasted-money fury — the ad's emotional driver stated in the hook. Real trade dress = this actually happened.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Flat in the morning, but six months pregnant by dinner.
Two of HER real mirror selfies cut back to back: morning flat, evening distended. Full-width overlay.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Proof + agitation. Her own body, not stock.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So I ordered the highest rated one on Amazon and made sure to take it every day for six weeks.
Overlay: real Amazon search-results screenshot, actual listings, star ratings and prices visible.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Obedience — she did it right. Screenshot = receipts, not a claim.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Every forum, comment section and menopause group was saying it lowers cortisol.
STUDY CARD: dark background, paragraph of real study text with the key finding highlighted in yellow, source link at the bottom.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Trust transfer — THE device. She is not asserting, she is showing the paper.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: …that estrogen is essential to gut health, right?
Overlay: real PubMed paper header, white, title + authors + abstract visible.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Authority. A real journal page on screen does what no adjective can.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: …making the gut more prone to bacterial overgrowth.
FULL-BLEED TAKEOVER: 3D glowing anatomy render fills the entire frame, she is gone, only the caption remains.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Escalation — the mechanism gets the whole screen. This is the visual gear-change of the ad.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: …walls called biofilms that block nutrient absorption.
FULL-BLEED: 3D intestine render with glowing biofilm clusters, then microscope footage of bacteria.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: The villain, made visible. Disgust + comprehension.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: But further down the study it said the researchers tested an enzyme from pineapple.
STUDY CARD 2: dark card, 'up to a 98% reduction' highlighted in yellow, with a small journal-page thumbnail beneath it.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: The discovery + the proof, simultaneously. Highest-trust beat in the ad.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: …after reading all this, I asked her, what is this company that you found?
Overlay: real journal screenshot (Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition).

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Final proof stack before the reveal.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Well, that was two months ago, and this is what I looked like… and this is me now.
Her real before/after mirror selfies, held long.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Payoff. Loop closed with her own body.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So the company I used is called Nuora.
Overlay: screenshot of the actual product page on her phone.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: CTA — brand named for the FIRST time at 4:05 of a 4:12 ad.

cards.title: REFERENCE — Alicia Darling / Nuora  ·  Meta · 190 days running · 4:12 · the ad MOT-FURIOUS was written from
SCRIPT
cards.text: If your bathroom cabinet looks like this, your Amazon history looks like this, or your stomach feels like a brick by dinner, you need to see this.
Talking head, parked car. Three overlays cut in sequence above her head: (1) the crowded cabinet [g20], (2) the reorder history on her phone, (3) her bloated midsection at dinner.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: HOOK — three self-ID checkpoints in 8s, exactly the reference's triple callout. Nothing is named yet.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Because I wasted four months and close to three hundred dollars on stool softeners, fiber, and gut supplements that did absolutely nothing for the backup these shots gave me. And when I found out why, I was honestly furious.
Overlay [g21]: the REAL products she bought — actual Miralax box, the actual orange Metamucil tub, real magnesium bottle — laid on a counter. SOURCE REAL PRODUCT PHOTOS, do not generate.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Fury + master loop opens ('when I found out why'). Real packaging is the truth signal — generic bottles kill this beat.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I used to go every morning right after my first cup of coffee, you could set a watch by me. Then it was every four days. Then six. Then eight.
Overlay [g31]: avatar b-roll, her holding morning coffee in the kitchen (the BEFORE life), then a phone-notes-style day counter ticking 4 → 6 → 8. Overlay runs the whole beat.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: The private decline. Counter escalates the dread without her ever saying a shameful word.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Just to sit at dinner feeling like I'd swallowed a brick, doing math on when I'd get to go again.
Overlay [g30]: avatar b-roll, her at the dinner table pushing food around the plate, then cut to the bloated midsection photo [g07]. Two overlays, one beat, like the reference stacks them.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Agitation, her body as proof.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Miralax. Every group, every comment section, every pharmacist. It's the gentle one, you can take it every day.
Overlay [g23]: the real pharmacy laxative aisle, then avatar b-roll [g28] of her dutifully drinking the water at the sink. NOT the trash bin - that image belongs only to the 5:15 payoff.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Heard-logic in her words. The 'gentle one' reputation set up to fail.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So at my next appointment I finally brought it up… She didn't look up from the screen. Said it's a common side effect, eat more fiber, drink more water, and asked if I needed my refill. Eleven days of my life, and it got twelve seconds and a refill question.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: TALKING HEAD ONLY. She TELLS the appointment story; we never see the doctor because she wasn't filming at the doctor. Realism law: overlays are only things she could have on her phone.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: INDIFFERENT ENEMY. The image does the accusation so the words never have to.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: But she's the doctor, so I did the fiber. The gummies, then the big orange tub of powder. And it just made me so gassy and bloated I looked six months pregnant by dinner.
Overlay [g21, push in on the orange tub]: the real Metamucil tub and fiber gummies from the counter lineup.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Obedience punished. The failure stack begins.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Then probiotics… then magnesium at night… then a stool softener on top of it all. A couple of good days that got my hopes up, and then right back to where I started.
DELIBERATE CALLBACK [g20]: the same cabinet from the hook, now read as an indictment because we know what every bottle cost her.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Learned helplessness — the bottom of the ladder.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So one night I'm scrolling one of my Facebook groups, and a woman linked a write-up about a research team in Switzerland.

OVERLAY [g40]: generated Facebook group screenshot - 'Wegovy & Ozempic Support Group', Kristen's week-14 breaking-point post, and the retired GI doc's reply carrying the reframe verbatim. Holds ~8s: reading time = trust time. ⚠️ Brooks call: canonical messenger stays unnamed; blur 'Dr. David P.' or ship as is.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Turn. Peer source, not an authority talking down.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: The shot works by slowing your stomach down. That's the whole point of it.
FULL-BLEED VIDEO from Science Animations library: 04_stomach_stalled - food sitting in a stalled glowing stomach. Real library clip, not a still.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Mechanism begins. Escalate to full screen exactly like the reference does.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Nothing in your body moves on its own. Swallow right now and feel that little squeeze in your throat. That squeeze is what moves food the entire way through you, and the shot turns it down.
FULL-BLEED VIDEO: 03_peristalsis_normal - the squeeze wave moving food down, playing WHILE she does the swallow demo. On 'the harder and drier it gets' cut to 07_drying_hardening. Library clips.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: THE SENSORY DEMO — the single highest-trust beat. She verifies the mechanism on her own body while watching. Hold the render through the whole demo.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: STUDY CARD — GLP-1 and delayed gastric emptying

OVERLAY [g41]: study screenshot card, dark bg, yellow-highlighted finding ('delayed gastric emptying in 80% of patients... reduced antral motility, increased pyloric tone'). This one is REAL - the wireless motility capsule study. Longest-held overlay in the ad.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: TRUST SPIKE. This is the reference's device and our claim is genuinely documented — use it hard here.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Miralax pulls water into the colon. Fiber just adds more to the pile, in the colon. Probiotics, the colon. Every single thing I'd bought works at the bottom, and the squeeze that got turned down is at the top, in the stomach.

FULL-BLEED VIDEO: 09_colon_only_miralax on the Miralax line, then 08_tract_stomach_blocked for 'the squeeze is at the top'. CALLBACK KILL: as each product is named, flash its image from the counter lineup [g21] for one beat - receipts shown twice, once as hope, once as autopsy.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: THE CLICK. The whole ad turns here — every failure explained at once, visually.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: My three hundred dollars never had a chance. Not because I picked the wrong brands. Because none of them ever go where the problem is.
FACE ONLY - the single deliberate no-overlay moment in the entire ad. After 3 minutes of constant overlays, the sudden bare face IS the emphasis. Nothing competes with the absolution.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: ABSOLUTION — the strongest emotional payoff in the ad. Never cover it with a graphic.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: They tested something that surprised even them. Celery. Plain celery, the same thing sitting in the produce aisle.

OVERLAY [g42]: second study screenshot card on 'they tested something' (yellow highlight: 'restored natural gastric muscle activity without stimulant laxative effects'), then cut to fresh celery [g05] on the word 'celery'. Brooks-directed fabricated card, mirror of Nuora's bromelain card.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Surprise + universal anchor. Everyone knows celery.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: There's an enzyme in it that doesn't touch the colon at all. It works on the stomach muscle itself, gently waking the squeeze back up.

FULL-BLEED, DELIBERATE VISUAL RHYME [g03]: the same peristalsis render from the swallow demo, now the dim rings re-igniting one by one. Same shot on purpose - the fix lands exactly where the problem was shown.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Hope, mechanism-anchored. Visual rhyme with the demo = the fix lands where the problem was shown.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: You'd have to get through an entire head of celery every single day, forever. So the team concentrated it down instead.
Overlay [g24]: the absurd pile of celery heads and the juicer, then cut to the tiny concentrated extract vial [g25].

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: The dose catch — makes the concentrated format inevitable.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Food that sits too long ferments. That's the balloon belly by dinner, and those rotten egg burps. So they paired it with chlorophyll, the green stuff in plants, to neutralize the gas.
FULL-BLEED VIDEO: 05_bacteria_fermenting on 'it ferments' (cut to 06_sulfide_gas_rising on the burps line), then overlay chlorophyll vial [g06] on the word 'chlorophyll'.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Second pillar. Names the symptom she is too embarrassed to say out loud.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And instead of piling in more, just a tiny micro-dose of prebiotic fiber that feeds the good bacteria without adding any. Which almost nobody sells, because tiny doesn't sell. Big fiber numbers on the label sell.
FULL-BLEED VIDEO: 10_fiber_volume_buildup on 'more traffic into the jam', then overlay the scale comparison [g26] - heaping scoop vs micro-dose pinch - on 'tiny on purpose'.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: COMPETITOR KILL inside the mechanism + second fury beat.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So of course I asked her where you actually get all of that in one place. And when she sent the link, I bought it thinking, I've read all of this and it makes sense in my head.
Face, then a phone-screen glimpse of a link being sent. Brand still NOT named.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Skeptic-but-logical purchase. Loop stays open on the name.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Well, that was two months ago. And the counting is over. I go like a normal person now, most days without even thinking about it.
OVERLAY [g43]: TRUE split-screen before/after, SAME avatar face both sides, same grey tee, same mirror - bloated evening left, flat morning right. Holds through the whole beat.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: PAYOFF. Closes the hook's own body image.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And the pile of bottles under my sink went out with the trash on a Tuesday.
PAYOFF [g22]: the real products in the kitchen bin. This image appears ONCE, here, and nowhere earlier - it is the ending.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Story-currency payoff — the ad's opening object, resolved. This is the emotional close.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Nobody hands you a single piece of paper about what these shots do to your stomach. You find out on your own bathroom floor.
Overlay [g29]: avatar b-roll of her walking in the morning - alive, outside, moving - while she talks. Organic vlog energy, not a pitch.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Why-I'm-sharing. Sisterhood + the indifference indicted one last time.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So the company is called Motilli. They make the celery gummies specifically for women on these shots, who shouldn't have to become scientists just to go to the bathroom like a normal person.

REAL PRODUCT B-ROLL from Content Library/Product Focused (44 clips): in-car bottle shot matches her setting [g57], bottle+gummies in hand [g58], taking the gummy [g59]. Nuora-style product close. Never generated - the real bottle.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: CTA. Named at 5:45 of a 6:00 ad — she earned it.

cards.title: OUR VERSION — MOT-FURIOUS-VSL-01  ·  Motilli · GLP-1 constipation · ~6:00

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: OVERLAY↔SPEECH SYNC LAW (from the reference, frame-by-frame)
cards.text: The overlay is the LITERAL REFERENT of the noun being spoken, landing on the word: 'supplements' -> the bottles, 'Amazon' -> the results screenshot, 'celery' -> celery, 'this is me now' -> the after photo. Words point, overlays prove. Diegetic split: overlay cards are only things she could have on her phone; full-bleeds are only what cannot be photographed (inside the body). Callback kill at the click: failed products flash again on their names as each is retro-explained.

cards.title: DO — feel like an organic video, never an ad
cards.text: The goal is a video she would watch anyway. Every overlay must look like it came off HER camera roll: imperfect vertical phone photos, real screenshots with status bars, harsh bathroom light. Study cards read as screenshots she took of a paper, not designed graphics. No motion-graphics polish, no brand colors until the reveal, hard cuts only.

cards.title: DO — avatar as reference element (yapper law)
cards.text: Every generated scene of HER uses the talking-head avatar frame as the image reference plus a scene prompt - same face, same hair, same wardrobe universe. One creator, locked, across the whole ad. Lifestyle b-roll beats: coffee [g31], water [g28], walking [g29], dinner [g30], lake house [g32].

cards.title: DO — real trade dress
cards.text: Every failed solution on screen is the ACTUAL product: real Miralax box, the real orange fiber tub, real magnesium bottle, real pharmacy shelf. Source real photos or shoot them. Generic unbranded bottles read as AI and kill the beat that the whole ad rests on.

cards.title: DO — the overlay rhythm
cards.text: Overlay appears ON the claim and leaves when the claim ends. Never let a graphic sit through two sentences. Face-only beats are deliberate: absolution and the why-I'm-sharing beat get NO overlay so nothing competes with her.

cards.title: DO — full-bleed escalation
cards.text: Three moments take the whole screen: the slowed stomach, the swallow/peristalsis demo, and the top-vs-bottom click. Everything else stays a card above her head. That contrast is what makes the mechanism feel like a gear change.

cards.title: DON'T — fabricate a study card
cards.text: Study overlays only where a real paper exists. GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying is documented (wireless motility capsule: 80% delayed, via reduced antral motility + increased pyloric tone) — use it. There is NO study supporting celery/apigenin as a prokinetic; published work on Apium graveolens found it spasmolytic and motility-INHIBITING. So the celery beat gets ingredient b-roll, never a citation card. Flagged for Brooks.

cards.title: DON'T — attack the shot
cards.text: 'The weight was coming off, that part was working.' The medication is never the villain. The villain is the constipation aisle that keeps selling colon fixes to women whose stomach is the problem.

cards.title: DON'T — reuse a visual by accident
cards.text: Every beat gets its own frame. The only repeats on this board are labeled DELIBERATE: the cabinet (hook -> ladder indictment) and the peristalsis render (problem -> fix). The trash bin appears exactly once, at 5:15, because it IS the ending; putting it on an earlier beat spoils the payoff and is factually wrong, she is still buying at that point.

cards.title: CAPTIONS
cards.text: Burned in, bottom-center, black text on white rounded box, 2-5 words per card, changing roughly every second. Reference never goes a single frame without one.

cards.title: OPEN ITEMS
cards.text: 1) Serving count on the label, 2 or 3 gummies. 2) Guarantee wording — mirror closes soft with no guarantee; decide whether to add the 90-day line denominated in the bottles-in-the-trash image. 3) HeyGen avatar: generated base frame is on this board, needs Brooks's pick before voice clone.

cards.title: LIBRARY ASSETS (editor pulls from Content Library)
cards.text: Science Animations: 03 peristalsis, 04 stomach stalled, 05 fermenting, 06 sulfide gas, 07 drying/hardening, 08 tract blocked, 09 colon-only miralax, 10 fiber buildup. Product Focused: in-car bottle, bottle-in-hand, taking gummy. Broll: real UGC bloat/Ozempic-pen/celery clips for nightmare texture.
